title: Théorie arithmétique. Théorie de Galois des motifs (1965) : notes manuscites (s.d.), tapuscrit (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: notes on the Galois theory of motives, around 1965. X is a base, probably a scheme. For each 'type' α there is a category ℳ_α of motives over X, presumably finitely generated so that its tensor-automorphism groups are of finite type. T_α(k) is the set of fibre functors on ℳ_α with values in projective modules over a ring k. The page title is 'Groupes fondamentaux motiviques discrets'.

(1) Integral fibre functors. For a fibre functor ξ with values in ℤ-modules (the model is Betti cohomology with ℤ coefficients), Grothendieck defines the 'discrete motivic fundamental group' π_1(X,ξ) := Aut^⊗(ξ) = G_ξ(ℤ). Here G_ξ = Aut^⊗(ξ) is an affine group scheme over ℤ: an integral form of the motivic Galois or fundamental group. π_1 is then an arithmetic group inside it.

(2) Finiteness. The N.B. says that, by Borel–Harish-Chandra, there are only finitely many ξ in T_α(ℤ) for fixed α, implicitly up to isomorphism. So there are only finitely many discrete fundamental groups. The mechanism is the following. Two ℤ-fibre functors are mutually torsors under G_ξ. Forms that agree over ℚ and over ℤ_p are counted by a double-coset (class number) set G(ℚ)\G(𝔸_f)/∏G(ℤ_p), which is finite by Borel (1963) and Borel–Harish-Chandra (1962).

(3) An open question. He then asks: 'Sont-ils tous [réalisés/motivés] à des places ??' My reading is that he asks whether every member of this finite set of ℤ-forms arises from a Betti realization at some archimedean place, i.e. a complex embedding, possibly with a base point. Betti lattices at different complex embeddings of a number field all become isomorphic over Ẑ via étale comparison. So they lie in a single 'genus' of ℤ-fibre functors. The question is whether the genus is exhausted by places, and conversely the page implicitly notes that different places can give non-isomorphic discrete groups.

(4) General ring k. For ξ in T_α(k), the fibre of a motive M at ξ is M_ξ = ξ(M). He sets π_1(X,ξ) = Aut(ξ), an abstract group, and G(X,ξ) = Aut-underline(ξ), the k-group scheme, with π_1(X,ξ) ≅ G(X,ξ)(k).

(5) Comparison with topology. He proposes comparing with π_1(X^an, x) when ξ comes from a fibre at a point. Every motive over X gives a ℤ-local system on X^an, so there is a monodromy homomorphism π_1^top(X^an,x) → G(X,ξ_x)(ℤ).

(6) Example: Hodge structure on the fundamental group. Take X connected over ℂ and ξ the Betti fibre at a point x in X(ℂ). Then ξ_ℂ carries a filtration (the Hodge filtration), and ξ factors through (filtered, or Hodge) modules. Consequently π_1(X,ξ), or rather its coordinate ring, inherits a Hodge structure or filtrations. In modern terms: the coordinate ring of Aut^⊗(ξ) is colim ξ(M)^∨ ⊗ ξ(M). If ξ lifts to mixed Hodge structures, this colimit is an ind-mixed-Hodge-structure, so the motivic fundamental group at x carries a mixed Hodge structure.
errors: The finiteness claim needs hypotheses that are not stated. G_ξ must be a ℤ-group scheme of finite type with reductive-type behaviour for the Borel–Harish-Chandra or Borel–Serre finiteness to apply. The claim must also be read up to isomorphism of fibre functors.

The real and rational classes must also be controlled. Borel's class-number finiteness counts forms within a fixed ℚ-form, i.e. a 'genus'. The full set of ℤ-points of a torsor gerbe additionally requires finiteness of H^1(ℤ,G) (fppf), which holds for smooth affine G over ℤ but is not automatic for arbitrary flat G_ξ.
Notational slip: π_1(X,ξ)_0 ≃ G(X,ξ)(k) is just the definition restated. The subscript is unclear, perhaps a deleted 'k'.

The Hodge statement is only sketched. Strictly, it is the affine ring (or Lie algebra) of G(X,ξ) that carries an ind-mixed Hodge structure, not the abstract group π_1. In general one gets a mixed rather than a pure Hodge structure.

ideas.what: Integral (discrete) motivic fundamental group π_1(X,ξ) = Aut^⊗(ξ) = G_ξ(ℤ) for a ℤ-valued fibre functor on motives over X
ideas.modern_name: ℤ-points of an integral form of the motivic Galois or fundamental group (Tannakian group over ℤ; cf. Nori motives with integral coefficients, Ayoub's motivic Galois groups)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Tannakian formalism over rings: Saavedra Rivano (1972), Deligne (1990); integral motivic Galois groups: Nori, Ayoub (2010s)
ideas.where_published: Grothendieck's motivic Galois group idea appears only through Saavedra and Récoltes et Semailles; the integral 'discrete' version is not, to my knowledge, published

ideas.what: Finiteness of the set of ℤ-fibre functors of given type via Borel–Harish-Chandra class-number finiteness
ideas.modern_name: Finiteness of genus / class number of arithmetic groups applied to torsors of ℤ-forms of the motivic group
ideas.usually_credited_to: Borel–Harish-Chandra (1962), Borel (1963), Borel–Serre (1964) for Galois cohomology finiteness

ideas.what: Question whether all integral fibre functors (discrete fundamental groups) come from Betti realizations at (archimedean) places
ideas.modern_name: Genus versus class for Betti lattices of conjugate varieties; integral comparison across complex embeddings
ideas.usually_credited_to: Serre (1964, non-homeomorphic conjugate varieties); Milne–Suh (2010, nonhomeomorphic conjugates of Shimura varieties via genus arguments)

ideas.what: Comparison of the motivic π_1 at a point with the topological π_1(X^an,x) via monodromy of motivic local systems
ideas.modern_name: Monodromy representation into the motivic or Mumford–Tate group; geometric part of the motivic fundamental group
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne (Hodge II, 1971), André (1992, theorem of the fixed part), Ayoub, Nori

ideas.what: The fibre functor at a complex point is filtered or Hodge-valued, so the fundamental group (its coordinate ring) inherits a Hodge structure or filtration
ideas.modern_name: Mixed Hodge structure on fundamental groups / relative completions / motivic fundamental groups
ideas.usually_credited_to: Morgan (1978), Hain (1987; relative completion 1998), Deligne (1989, P^1 minus 3 points); Simpson (1992) for C^*-action on the pro-algebraic π_1

missed.claim: As early as about 1965, Grothendieck links the motivic fundamental group to Hodge theory: the Betti fibre functor at a complex point is filtered, so π_1 carries a Hodge structure or filtration. This is the Tannakian mechanism (Hodge structure on the coordinate ring of Aut^⊗ of a Hodge-valued fibre functor) later used by Hain and Deligne. Morgan's and Hain's work, and Deligne's 1989 motivic π_1, are not usually traced to a 1965 Grothendieck note.
missed.quote: Le foncteur ξ_ℂ a une structure filtrée ... donne π_1(X,ξ) muni d'une structure de Hodge ou de filtrations
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is historical priority for the idea of Hodge structures on (motivic) fundamental groups. It applies to the full motivic π_1 of X, not only its unipotent completion, which is closer to Ayoub's and Nori's relative motivic groups than to the classical Malcev picture.

missed.claim: He poses an open question: is the finite set of integral (discrete) motivic fundamental groups, i.e. ℤ-fibre functors in a genus, entirely realized by Betti fibre functors at places, i.e. complex embeddings? This frames conjugate varieties with non-isomorphic but profinitely isomorphic π_1 as genus versus class of ℤ-forms of the motivic group.
missed.quote: Donc un ensemble fini de groupes fondamentaux discrets. Sont-ils tous [réalisés] à des places ??
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Milne–Suh and work on Galois conjugates with distinct π_1 use exactly class-number and genus arguments in special cases. A general surjectivity question (do places exhaust the genus of integral motivic fibre functors?) does not seem to be formulated in the literature.

missed.claim: He proposes a 'discrete motivic fundamental group' G_ξ(ℤ), an arithmetic group attached to an integral fibre functor on motives over X, together with its comparison to π_1^top. This integral or arithmetic-group viewpoint on motivic π_1 was not systematically developed.
missed.quote: Soit ξ ∈ T(ℤ), on pose π_1(X,ξ) = Aut(ξ) = G_ξ(ℤ)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It connects to current interest in integral motivic Galois groups and in the arithmeticity of monodromy groups of motivic local systems (the integral Mumford–Tate conjecture and arithmeticity questions).

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a brief sketch. It contains two notable early ideas: a Hodge structure on the motivic fundamental group, anticipating Morgan, Hain and Deligne by over a decade, and a genus/class-number viewpoint on integral Betti fibre functors at different places, with an open question about whether places exhaust the genus. Both are suggestive and plausibly undocumented as Grothendieck's, but neither is worked out.
transcription_corrections: Line 3 should read 'N.B. En vertu de Borel–Harish-Chandra, il n'y a qu'un nombre fini de ξ ∈ T_α(ℤ) possibles, pour α donné' ('Harish-Chandra' is inserted above the line).
The question 'Sont-ils tous motivés à des places ??' is uncertain. The word read as 'motivés' could be 'réalisés' or 'trouvés'. The struck word before 'places' looks like 'classes'.
'π_1(X,ξ)_0' is uncertain; the subscript may be a slip or 'k'.

The second-to-last line is better read as 'ξ considéré comme foncteur à valeurs dans les modules filtrés', followed by 'donne π_1(X,ξ) muni d'une structure de Hodge ou de filtrés...'. Here 'Hodge' is underlined.
